$comment: Checksum amnesty for comment-only edits to already-applied migrations. Each entry maps a migration filename to sha256 checksums the file PREVIOUSLY had when it was applied to some database. When db:push finds a stored checksum that matches a listed prior checksum, it updates the stored checksum to the current file's checksum and skips re-applying, instead of failing with 'changed after it was applied'. This is NOT a license to edit migration SQL semantics: an amnesty entry is only valid for comment/whitespace-only edits, and every entry must be code-reviewed with a reason explaining why the edit happened. Editing applied migration SQL is still forbidden — add a new migration instead.
